story.title: Cold Comfort
story.blurb: Zion's log from five days into being stranded on a frozen planet, with a sealed airlock, a garbled radio and a crew that is starting to come apart.

lines.text: It’s been about five days since we got here.

I spent the entire first night waiting to be blown up by a planet-buster, but it didn’t happen. We never saw those rodent sprites again. They threatened us, held a planet hostage, kidnapped a crewmate, and then just… left. Left us to die.

Despite our best efforts, we haven’t made any progress on the ship. The only exposed entrance, the airlock, has completely frozen shut, meaning we can’t move the ship nor pilot it anywhere. Contacting the outside world is out of the question, too. Every time I have attempted to call Mission Control—and believe me, I have tried—everything I hear back is garbled. There’s no way of knowing if my messages are being received or not.

Morra is kind-of losing their mind, I think. After barely being cognizant when we got here, they have only gone further down the deep end. They’re scatterbrained, can’t decide what to do, can’t remember where they are. Morra spends at least an hour every day trying to wormhole off of the planet, to no success obviously.

I’ve hypothesized that there’s some strong magnetic field on this planet. It’s the only thing that could explain all the abnormalities; the ship randomly crashing, random flybys of the unmanned ship (I thought it was a runaway spectre at first), Morra’s teleportation failure… oh, and the aurorae littering the sky. I have to admit, though, it’s quite beautiful to look at. Bellow would enjoy it.

Speaking of Bellow… I don’t think he’s doing too well. The threat of his planet’s destruction, coupled with losing Zach… I think it hit him hard. He hasn’t had any real danger during this mission. I mean, he’s been mortally wounded, but we’re always a short walk away from a healing pod or special meds. This… this is different.

lines.text: No amount of medicine will cure that kind of despair.

Although, as frustrating as it is to lose a crew member… I think Zach is safer with his dad than he is here. Every day it’s like we spiral closer to our collective demise. You’d think with all the infrastructure we’ve built here that we’d be safer, but no…
This is all because of Seth.

Out of everyone, he might be in the worst condition. Although it’s hard to tell, because he’s already insane. He keeps shambling around, mumbling about lancers and shadows and friends. I guess losing his bee partner messed him up more than usual, but does that really justify sabotaging our every attempt at survival?

We’re lucky that there’s a tundra nearby, otherwise we’d be as good as dead. Dutch and I have spent most of our time gathering wood and other materials. It’s monotonous but doesn’t bother me. It’s actually kind-of spawned a game between me and Dutch to see who can carry more at once. Or, at least, that’s what we made up to distract from the chaos back at base.

Speaking of which, our “base” is functional, but kind of a mess. Morra built most of it here and there while dissociating. Hell, they spent three hours floating and tying sticks together to help us out of that pit in the first place. The underground lab (if you can even call it that) is where Bellow hides most of the time. He’s always down there, writing in his journal or trying to grow things in what I can only assume to be a desperate attempt at normalcy. At least he’s helping grow food…
It’s dissonant here. No one wants to talk, and when we do, most of the time it results in a screaming match. I suppose that’s to be expected in a time of crisis, but I can’t help thinking…
It feels like our crew is falling apart.
